feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Unconditionally removing OP_MASKs from transaction scripts would create a vulnerability unless an explicit indicator is included to demonstrate their removal. This is due to the potential for a mismatch between the visible script and the actual "real script" that might still contain OP_MASKs, posing risks of unexpected behavior or exploitation.
One approach to mitigate this issue involves having the signature commit directly to the output script. However, this solution is not considered ideal, as it introduces complexity without addressing the underlying concerns in a robust manner. In contrast, the Eltoo protocol does not require changes to the script during rebinding, making it inherently less susceptible to this class of issues, unless there have been recent modifications to its design.
When utilizing SIGHASH_NOINPUT, developers must exercise caution regarding key reuse, as the absence of input commitment could enable unintended interactions if keys are reused across different scenarios. The safety of such approaches cannot be fully evaluated without a finalized taproot proposal, as current assumptions may not hold under future implementations. Nevertheless, if a signature explicitly indicates the use of a taproot script, the level of security remains at least as strong as previous methods, potentially offering greater flexibility and generality.
For further exploration of these concepts and technical proposals, refer to the ongoing discussions within the Bitcoin development community.
